label: input g in the first five original positions
explanation: Token-detector for the letter g in the original phase. It fires whenever the input is g at steps t=0..4, and essentially never anywhere else. Every such step fires (dev precision 1.0, recall 0.997). It does not fire on any other token, on g at original positions 5 or later, on the delimiter, or on g fed back during the copy phase (only 236 copy-phase activations). Magnitude depends on position. At t=0..2 it is strong and near-maximal (~2.0 of max 2.27). It is weaker at t=3, and weak at t=4 (mean ~0.37, about 3% of activation mass). A repeated g, i.e. not the first occurrence, fires somewhat more weakly (e.g. 0.88 vs 1.0 of max). Sequence length L and the surrounding tokens have little effect beyond this.

issues: Minor: the 212 test misses (dev: 236) are systematic but tiny. They are copy-phase steps at t=5 where a g that sat at original index 1 in a sequence with L=3 is fed back (e.g. 'p g q <DEL> p [g:0.14]'). Activations are 0.02-0.14 of max and hold 0.0% of mass, so they don't affect the label.

Magnitude claims check out roughly: estimated mean at t=4 is about 0.30 (explanation says about 0.37), and t=4 holds 3.1% of mass. Repeated g: 6.2% of activations but 4.6% of mass, so it really is somewhat weaker.
There are zero activations at original index >= 5 and none on the delimiter. Test precision is 1.0 with no false positives, so the label does not overclaim.
